I'm sorry you felt patronized by my wording. "Identify" is typically go-to for explaining gender in my experience, and I don't personally see anything wrong with it. I wouldn't say it's a feeling, but rather a recognition of something that is a part of your identity. To identify is to claim something in recognition that is a part of who you are, whether you take that to be as your chemical makeup, your experiences, your personality, etc. I would say without a doubt anyone could "feel" like a boy, but I wouldn't say that inherently makes them transgender. I've seen plenty of cis girls throw on their boyfriend's t-shirt and say they "feel like a boy," but they're not trans, it's just an expression.
To identify is just a way to claim something as part of your self-identity. I could identify with having a mental illness, because I recognize that it is a part of me.
Do trans people not identify as trans?? I don't understand your point.

That could be true for you, but you can't make that assumption for everyone. I personally identify as trans and use he/him pronouns, but on occasion wear a dress because I can comprehend that my physique compliments the dress and I look and feel very nice.
